turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Good afternoon. Could you tell me how old you are?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I'm sixty-six years old. I still feel like I'm fifty, though.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Ha, I hear that a lot. Are you married, single, widowed?

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Are you a Canadian citizen, or a permanent resident?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I'm a permanent resident. I haven't taken citizenship yet.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: How long have you lived in Canada, if you don't mind me asking?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Since I turned eighteen, I've lived in Canada for twenty-two years, sorry, it's actually twenty-five.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Okay, and what's your income right now?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Old Age Security and a small pension together come to about nine thousand a year.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Do you receive the Old Age Security payment?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yes, I get the Old Age Security every month.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: When did you last file your taxes?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I filed last year, for 2025. My nephew helps me with it.
